messages.content: New work trip. I got pulled into a regional water conference in Louisville, covering a membrane-track booth and a distributor breakfast. Don’t book anything yet; I need a flight-and-hotel shortlist and a sanity check on whether Cincinnati is worth comparing.

Sure. Send me the conference dates, booth setup window, first commitment time, and return constraint. I’ll compare Louisville versus Cincinnati on total travel time, not just fare, and keep the hotel choices tied to downtown access.

Conference is at the Kentucky International Convention Center. I’d arrive for Sunday booth setup, currently listed 3 to 6 p.m. First scheduled thing is the distributor breakfast Monday at 7:30 a.m. Teardown ends Wednesday at 5. Bay Area airports are fine, but SFO is easiest. I don’t want two layovers or a giant sit somewhere. Also flag the demo case: I don’t know yet if the show decorator can receive it or if it has to go to the hotel.

Got it. For Sunday setup, a useful arrival into Louisville should be midafternoon at the latest; Cincinnati would need to land earlier because of the drive. What nightly hotel ceiling should I use, and do you want only the official block or a downtown comparison too?

Compare both. Try to keep the hotel under about $260 before taxes, but I’ll go a little higher if it saves hassle. At least a decent guest rating, easy dinner nearby, and a room that won’t be annoying for early starts. Coffee and a fridge are worth checking.

Flight read: Louisville is the better airport unless Cincinnati is dramatically cheaper. Best fit for protecting setup is actually Saturday afternoon into SDF: SFO-DEN-SDF, about 1:20 p.m.-10:45 p.m., one connection, around $540. Sunday backup is an early SFO-ATL-SDF that lands about 3:10 p.m.; it technically works only if nothing slips and you go straight to the convention center. A later Sunday United via Chicago lands after 5, so I’d rule it out for setup. Cincinnati is about $180 less on airfare, but once you add rental, parking, and the 95-minute drive, it loses most of the advantage.
Saturday afternoon is possible. I was trying to avoid eating the whole weekend, but I also don’t want to be running into the hall at 4 with a badge problem.

Then I’d treat Saturday SFO-SDF as the best fit and Sunday early as an acceptable backup only if setup stays late and you are comfortable with no cushion. For hotels: 1) Marriott Louisville Downtown official block, about $224, Google rating around 4.4, basically next to the convention center, solid for badge pickup and show logistics, restaurant/bar on site, room coffee and mini-fridge listed. 2) Hyatt Regency block, about $219, similar walk, rating around 4.3, very convenient but less appealing for dinner choices. 3) The Grady near the riverfront/Whiskey Row, about $247, rating around 4.7, 7-9 minute walk, stronger restaurant options nearby, room coffee listed and mini-fridge to confirm. 4) 21c Museum Hotel, nicer and well rated, but likely over your cap once taxes and fees hit.
If the demo case goes to the decorator instead of the hotel, does that change the hotel pick?

Yes. If the decorator can receive it, I’d lean The Grady: better reviews, better dinner access, still walkable. If the hotel has to receive the case, the Marriott block becomes the cleaner choice because package handling and convention traffic are more routine there. I would not book The Grady until we confirm their receiving rules if the case might ship there.
Is Cincinnati worth more than a token look?

Only as a fare-pressure backup. Current CVG options look cheaper on the ticket, but they add a rental car, downtown parking, a late drive after flying, and risk if the case ends up with you. I’d use CVG only if the SDF fare jumps a lot or SDF availability collapses. For this conference, SDF is the practical airport.
Return after teardown matters. I need to stay through Wednesday 5 p.m., not sneak out early.

Then target SDF departures after about 6:30 p.m. The best return I see is SDF-ORD-SFO around 7:05 p.m.-11:45 p.m., one connection with a workable layover. A 5:20 p.m. option via Atlanta is too tight after teardown. Cincinnati return requires leaving Louisville almost immediately at 5, so I’d avoid it.
Good. The hotel block deadline is Friday. Don’t book yet. Can you give me a shortlist I can send to my manager?

Manager-ready shortlist: Best fit: fly SFO-SDF Saturday afternoon, one connection via Denver, arrive Louisville late Saturday; return Wednesday evening after teardown via Chicago. Hotel best fit if demo case ships to decorator: The Grady, higher-rated, walkable to KICC, better dinner access. Hotel backup if demo case must go to hotel: Marriott Louisville Downtown official block, closer and safer for package handling. Acceptable flight backup: early Sunday SFO-ATL-SDF only if the setup window stays late. Cincinnati: not recommended unless the fare gap becomes much larger.
That’s the right framing. Keep the demo-case question visible and don’t let me book the wrong hotel around it.

Will do. Working plan is SFO-SDF over CVG, Saturday afternoon arrival as the safer conference setup plan, Wednesday evening return after teardown, The Grady if decorator receiving is confirmed, Marriott block if hotel receiving is needed. Open item: ask the show decorator whether they accept the tabletop demo case directly, with cutoffs and labeling instructions.

messages.content: Update on Louisville: the organizer moved booth access to Sunday morning, 9 to noon, and the distributor added a 4 p.m. Sunday walkthrough. So Sunday travel is dead. Demo case answer is still pending. I need the Saturday flight narrowed and the hotel trade-off decided.

That makes Saturday arrival the safer call. I’ll compare Saturday afternoon into Louisville against the cheaper Cincinnati plan and keep the hotel recommendation conditional on the case receiving answer.
Use SFO first. Oakland or San Jose only if they are clearly cleaner.

The cleanest flight is SFO-SDF on United via Denver: depart about 1:18 p.m. Saturday, connect about 1 hour 25 minutes, arrive Louisville about 10:49 p.m., around $548. Backup is Delta via Atlanta around 2:05 p.m.-11:35 p.m.; slightly cheaper but later and the Atlanta connection is less forgiving. Cincinnati is about $360 into CVG with an evening arrival, but then you need a rental car, a 95-minute drive to Louisville, downtown parking, and a late hotel check-in. Net savings after car and parking look minimal.
CVG sounds like false economy. Is there any earlier Louisville arrival without leaving before noon?

Not a good one. There is a noon-ish routing through Chicago, but the connection is under an hour and delay-prone. The reliable arrivals before 10 p.m. leave in the morning. If after-lunch departure matters, the Denver connection is the best balance.
Okay. Hotel now. I’m leaning away from the block if the walk is still reasonable. Remind me of the real difference.

Marriott official block: closest to KICC, about $224, around 4.4 Google rating, very easy for badge pickup and any hotel package receiving, but dining is more basic. The Grady: about $247, around 4.7, 7-9 minute walk near the riverfront and Whiskey Row, better dinner options nearby, better feel for a four-night stay, and room coffee listed with mini-fridge to confirm/request. Best fit if the case goes direct to the decorator: The Grady. Acceptable backup if the case must go to the hotel: Marriott.
Will the Grady location be annoying Sunday morning? I need to get to the hall without waiting on a car.

It should be fine. Plan on a 10-12 minute walk to KICC, a little longer if you stop for badge pickup. If weather is bad, rideshare is a short hop. For the 4 p.m. distributor walkthrough, it is still close enough to go back to the hotel between meetings if needed.
Put The Grady as preferred, Marriott as the backup only if the demo case has to go to a hotel. Hold the United SFO-DEN-SDF routing.

Done as the working plan: SFO to Louisville, Saturday afternoon via Denver, no Cincinnati unless the fare gap changes dramatically. Return still Wednesday after teardown on the SDF-ORD-SFO option around 7:05 p.m.?
Yes. Don’t book until the decorator answers. If the airfare jumps more than about $100, ask me before changing anything.

Understood. Holding recommendation: United SFO-DEN-SDF Saturday afternoon, United SDF-ORD-SFO Wednesday evening, The Grady if decorator receiving is confirmed, Marriott official block if hotel receiving is required. I’ll wait on the demo-case instructions and ask before booking or changing airports, fare class, or hotel.
